items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching requires concealment
Concealment demands deliberate effort
The mortal world contains lowest men
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: To what kind of recipient may this teaching rightly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Only a previously accomplished person tested for one year is a fit recipient.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being numbered
The ordinal is fifth
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter of the text from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the work that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of the Kaula teaching been known?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge
The knowledge concerns Kaula determination
Grace of the Kaula lord is the cause
items.inference: The Kaula determination is known through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what reality does the soul dissolve, and what is the full account?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The teacher is asked to explain fully where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality identified as that soul?
premises: That reality is supreme
That reality is partless and eternal
That reality is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The soul in its highest sense is the supreme, partless, eternal, and pure reality.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to haṃsa and the individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That supreme soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is also called the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is the haṃsa, the individual constituted by power.
uncertainties: The exact sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated within living beings?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
Living beings are the locus
The air is situated in all of them
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon its departure from the body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
The moment of leaving is decisive
It is then designated supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is called the supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and received according to traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes through succession
It is received by traditional transmission
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as it comes down through the lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the immediate efficacy of merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing alone is emphasized
The addressee is addressed directly
items.inference: Even mere hearing of this knowledge has significant effect.
uncertainties: The main clause continues in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is undertaken for six months
The practitioner is specified
The state attained is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains the state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The role of kāṣāyaṃ is syntactically ambiguous in isolation.
items.plain_english: If one practices for six months, one attains the ochre state free from bondage.

items.question: What twofold result follows from the prescribed practice of the soul?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases
The practitioner gains union with yogis
Both results follow the practice
items.inference: The practice yields freedom from all disease and communion with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, one attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: A teaching has been told
The content is the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the recipient
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To which resolved and fully endowed person may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have firm resolve
items.inference: This teaching should be given to a fully endowed person of firm resolve.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose resolve is firm.

items.question: Under what condition must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly valued
It originates from the yoginīs
Transmission is explicitly prohibited here
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching born of the yoginīs must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of sambhavam is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The body was struck by ignorance
A change is declared now
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: Now that the veil of ignorance is struck away, the body is declared pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the seeker now wish to hear?
premises: The seeker expresses a wish
The topic concerns time
The desired teaching is the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The seeker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed by this teaching?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
There is no doubt
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching will explain without doubt how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you; there is no doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: Why can even a wise person be consumed despite contact with the nectar's essence?
premises: The nectar's tip and essence are present
A burning condition occurs
Even the wise are affected
items.inference: Even a wise person can be burned when exposed to the intense essence of nectar.
uncertainties: The imagery is compressed and may be technical.
items.plain_english: Even the wise person is burned at the tip of nectar by the intensity of its essence.

items.question: What specific yogic action with the breath is prescribed at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: A position at tongue and palate root is specified
The breath is the object
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: One should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows when this breath practice is maintained for one full year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this discipline destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for one established in this practice?
premises: The body may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
The practice prevents poison from entering
items.inference: For such a practitioner, poison does not enter the body even after a great serpent bite.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
